items.claim_or_requirement: 02 Addendum 1 item 4: 'H4 is not supported because the peak height is low, not because the cusp is not unusually rounded'; the pre-registered H4 rule uses L - S as the cusp rounding
items.evidence: 02_seed30510_diagnostic.md:315 (the literal H4 row): '(L - S)(1600) = +0.00027 against p90_pack(L - S, 1600) = +0.00234, exceeds: False'; numbers.json rules.target.cusp_exceeds_p90 = false (cusp_rounding_1600 = 0.000268, p90_cusp_1600 = 0.002345) and n_L_below_p10_1225_1600 = 16. So under the pre-registered operationalisation (01_preregistration.md:75) BOTH clauses fail: the peak height is low AND the L - S cusp rounding does not exceed the pack's p90. 'Unusually rounded' holds only for the post hoc measures (cusp depth, smoothing-free remainder, section 7.2). The addendum sentence is therefore wrong for the pre-registered rule it names in the same item.
items.fix: Say that under the literal rule both clauses fail (L below p10 at 16 of 16 exports; L - S = 0.00027 < p90 0.00234), and that the 'rounded cusp' reading holds only for the post hoc remainder/cusp-depth measures.

The figure waveP_offline_trajectory.png shows A_ctrl200 non-monotone (peak 5.44e-4 at u1775). The true statement is that the pathwise arms fall by 18-24% (q50) and the PPO controls change by +28% (lr 3e-4) / -5% (lr 3e-5). A_detmean (5.2e-4 -> 4.4e-4) is left out of the sentence.
items.fix: Rephrase: 'falls clearly for the pathwise arms (to 3.9e-4 / 4.3e-4), little for A_ctrl200 (4.9e-4) and rises for A_ctrl200_lr3e-4 (6.6e-4)'.
